title: Add Terraform resources/modules for SIEM audit export destinations (S3, Splunk HEC, Datadog) + secret references
author: Diego Santos
description: Context: As part of the SIEM-ready audit export beta, enterprise onboarding needs a consistent IaC story for provisioning destination-side infra and handing Redwood a least-privilege credential reference (vs pasting secrets into Console). This PR adds a small set of Terraform modules and examples to configure audit export destinations for S3 delivery, Splunk HEC, and Datadog Logs intake, including opinionated secret storage (AWS Secrets Manager / SSM) and outputs that match the control-plane export config API fields. Scope: (1) modules/audit_export_destination_s3 for S3 bucket prefix layout + optional SSE-KMS + cross-account assume-role policy snippet; (2) modules/audit_export_destination_splunk_hec for storing HEC token as a secret and generating a Redwood destination payload (endpoint/index/source/sourcetype); (3) modules/audit_export_destination_datadog_logs for storing API key as a secret and generating a Redwood destination payload (site/endpoint + tags). Each module outputs a "destination_spec_json" string suitable for pasting into Redwood Console or piping into the control-plane API, and emits a "secret_ref" (ARN or SSM parameter name) instead of the secret value. Security notes: outputs are marked sensitive where appropriate; IAM policies default to least privilege; KMS key is optional but strongly recommended; we document egress allowlist requirements and explicitly avoid supporting arbitrary HTTP sinks in beta. This PR is targeted at Solutions Engineering / Customer Success doing enterprise onboarding for the beta cohort; it’s feature-flagged on the Redwood side and does not by itself enable exports.
commits: terraform: add audit export destination modules (s3/splunk/datadog)
docs: onboarding examples + README updates for SIEM audit export beta
security: mark outputs sensitive + tighten IAM defaults
chore: add minimal validation for inputs (region/site/host) + formatting
conversation: Benji Okafor (review): The destination_spec_json output is super helpful. Can we align field names to match the control-plane API exactly (destination.type, destination.config.*, secret_ref.*), so SEs don’t need to translate? Also, please call out that filters/backfill are configured in Redwood, not in these modules.

Diego Santos (author): Updated outputs to mirror the API naming (type/config/secret_ref) and expanded examples/README to clarify that filters/backfill are configured in Console/API. Also added a note that the modules only cover destination-side provisioning + secret reference creation.

Hanae Suzuki (review): Please ensure we never output the Splunk HEC token / Datadog API key as a plain-text output. Even with `sensitive = true`, it shows up in state and can leak in logs. Recommend taking token/key as input, storing it in Secrets Manager, and only outputting the secret ARN/parameter name. Also add guidance on rotation (update secret value; Redwood reads via secret_ref).
Diego Santos (author): Confirmed: we only output secret ARN/SSM parameter name. No module returns secret values. Added rotation guidance + clarified state implications in module READMEs.

Kevin Osei (review): For S3: default to SSE-S3 is fine, but for regulated customers we should recommend SSE-KMS with customer-managed key. Can we provide an example with KMS and explicitly restrict s3:PutObject to the bucket prefix? Also, does the cross-account role assume policy have ExternalId support?

Diego Santos (author): Added an SSE-KMS example (customer-managed key), restricted PutObject permissions to the configured prefix, and included optional external_id in assume role trust policy + docs. Default remains minimal to avoid breaking existing setups, but README strongly recommends KMS for enterprise.

Connor O'Brien (review): Rollout note: please reference the beta feature flag + tenant allowlist (ENG-5184). Even though this is terraform, Support needs to know this doesn’t enable export automatically. Also please add a quick "paste into Console" snippet in examples.
Diego Santos (author): Added explicit callout to tenant allowlist / feature flag gating + a "Console paste" snippet in examples/README. Linked INT-9012 for internal enablement workflow.
Hanae Suzuki (approval): LGTM after the sensitive output changes and rotation notes.
Kevin Osei (approval): Approved with the KMS example + external_id option. Thanks.
Benji Okafor (approval): Approved. Output format alignment looks good.

content:
PR Title: Add Terraform resources/modules for SIEM audit export destinations (S3, Splunk HEC, Datadog) + secret references

Summary
- Adds three new modules to help enterprise customers provision destination-side resources and pass Redwood a secret reference (not raw credentials).
- Includes examples for common beta onboarding paths, including S3 cross-account + SSE-KMS.
- Updates root README with a new "SIEM audit export beta" section and links to examples.

Motivation
Enterprise onboarding for the SIEM-ready audit export beta needs an IaC-friendly way to:
1) create/configure destination infrastructure (especially S3 delivery),
2) store destination credentials safely (Splunk HEC token / Datadog API key) without pasting into the UI, and
3) produce a destination config payload that matches Redwood’s control-plane API.

What’s included
1) modules/audit_export_destination_s3
- Provisions (or references) an S3 bucket and configures a prefix for audit export objects.
- Optional SSE-KMS support (recommended); example includes CMK and least-privilege PutObject to prefix.
- Optional cross-account assume-role trust policy with external_id support.
- Outputs: destination_spec_json (string), plus IAM snippets/role ARN outputs needed by Redwood-side adapter.

2) modules/audit_export_destination_splunk_hec
- Stores HEC token in AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) and outputs a secret_ref.
- Outputs destination_spec_json with endpoint/index/source/sourcetype, plus secret_ref.*.
- Notes on HEC rate limiting and recommended batching defaults (informational).

3) modules/audit_export_destination_datadog_logs
- Stores Datadog API key as secret and outputs secret_ref only.
- Outputs destination_spec_json with site/endpoint and tag defaults for audit categories.

Non-goals / clarifications
- This does not enable exports by itself. Exports remain gated by Redwood feature flags + tenant allowlist (ENG-5184).
- Filters/backfill windows/rollout policies are configured in Redwood Console / control-plane API, not Terraform.
- Beta only: no support for arbitrary HTTP sinks or Private/on-prem patterns in this repo (documented elsewhere).

Security considerations
- No module outputs raw secret material. Outputs are restricted to secret references (ARN/parameter name).
- S3 permissions default to least privilege and can be scoped to prefix.
- KMS usage is strongly recommended; module supports KMS key ARN input.
- Cross-account role trust policy includes optional external_id.

How to use
- See examples/audit-export/README.md for copy/paste snippets. Each example prints a destination_spec_json you can paste into Redwood Console (Audit Export Settings) or use in the control-plane export config API.

Testing
- terraform fmt/validate across modules and examples
- tflint
- checkov policy checks

Rollout
- Intended for SE/CS onboarding of beta customers. Coordinate enablement via internal runbook/INT-9012 and confirm tenant allowlist is set before expecting events to flow.

Refs
- Linear: ENG-5144, ENG-5151, ENG-5156, ENG-5184
- Beta readiness: PM-858
